author: JokerPilot
quote: How did a game that took 13 years to make fall this flat on its face at launch? Where the hell was Q&A? You even had two delays to “polish” things up. I’d be scared to see what those earlier builds looked like if this is supposed to be polished. The game struggles to run even in parts of the starting area where barely anything is happening. I’m just standing in a room with other prisoners and the frame rate turns into a slideshow. HOW? This is not the first time this happens, where the game decides to chug to the point you can barely move. I tried to check my phone as I watched it vanish from my character’s hand as he proceeded to fall through the ground. I’ve had NPCs drop out of the sky and objects float around like they’re in zero gravity. Gta 6 looks great, but it’s hard to appreciate the detail when the game keeps stuttering and you can watch textures and LODs slowly load right in front of you. Every time I start getting immersed, something breaks or pops in and pulls me right back out. And seriously, how are we still struggling to get a steady 30 FPS in a Rockstar game in 2026? Rockstar needs to invest in time to optimize their games better because if we aren't getting a locked 30fps, we should be getting at least a 60fps. Options for 60fps performance mode vs 30 fps quality mode.Then there’s the story. Lucia felt like my ankle monitor throughout the game. Between all the optional missions that keep popping up to please her, which I have zero interest in, and the restrictions on what I can do on my own, I can’t just play the game how I want. Can’t steal a car in your own neighborhood. Try somewhere else and you might get told you don’t have enough skill to steal one. They’ve taken away a lot of what makes GTA fun and what is in it got turned into a slog. The story barely holds together, fails to connect and makes it hard for player to care what is even happening. This is honestly just sad Rockstar. I hope the reviewers who handed out perfect 10s are freaking out reading what players have to say about this launch. Its showing how biased and the shill nature of their reviews, making them look extremely bad.  I’d take it back for a refund if I could. However, I paid for a download code in a box and got a game that can barely run without turning into a slideshow. Welcome to getting scammed in 2026!

author: JokerPilot
quote:
I’ve been a fan of Ocarina of Time since its original release on the N64. While I appreciated the 3DS remake, I felt it lost some of the original’s charm and visual identity while staying almost too faithful to its underlying design. It often felt like the same game carried over to a newer system, with few meaningful changes beyond its presentation.

Because of that, I was a little skeptical going into Ocarina of Time on the Switch 2. But stepping into Hyrule again felt exciting. It brought back that feeling of playing the original for the very first time. I wanted to explore every corner and speak to every NPC, and the inclusion of Zelda Notes gave the completionist in me even more reason to keep searching. 

The wealth of new dialogue adds depth to the characters and fills in gaps that the original’s 1998 script left players wondering about. Every dungeon has been rebuilt from the ground up, with changes to familiar layouts and puzzles that make them feel fresh while preserving their identity.

Combat has also received a welcome boost. Enemies have more health and new attacks, encouraging you to think more carefully about each encounter and make better use of the tools in your arsenal. There are more reasons to experiment, and familiar opponents feel threatening. The cutscenes and expanded storytelling bring new life to the adventure. Character moments carry more emotional weight without becoming overly drawn out, giving the cast room to shine while keeping the story moving.

Overall, this is a gorgeous remake, and the love and attention poured into its world and characters are clear throughout. The fact that Nintendo gave us a physical game on cart that plays on day 1, full complete game, no code in a box is a win for me and for those who prefer physical media when other companies are doing away with physical media.  For me, the only thing missing is Master Quest. If Nintendo adds it in a free update, this could be everything I could have wanted from a return to Ocarina of Time.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: JokerPilot
quote:
If you're a fan of the classic or even a newcomer to the game, this is the game for you. They had done a fantastic job not only preserving the original but improving upon it. They added so many options for players, new controller schemes or ones mimicking the SNES version. Updated sound track but also offer the option to play with the original SNES music. There is a monster journal to keep track of weaknesses of enemies and specials they have as well as a map in the main menu that you can use to quickly leave an area and go somewhere else. The game holds a very stable framerate of 60fps with minimal drops mainly in the intro of the game for short segment.  The combat is fun and exciting, giving more incentive to get the command button pushes correctly as well as offering difficulty options for new beginners The visuals do the original game justice and I think anyone picking this up, old or new, will have a good time. 

PS: There is post game content with very challenging bosses!

author: JokerPilot
quote: Having just recently played botw going directly into Tears of the Kingdom, I was at first sceptical of the reusing of the same world but not anymore. Nintendo not only expanded upon the lore of the world but made it feel so different and alive that its exciting. The game feels fresh and new and caters to both old and new fans alike. With the day 1 patch, the fps has been very good and pretty smooth with minor dips in heavily populated areas but doesn't detract from the experience. The new mechanics are exciting and really open up on what you can do and how you traverse the world. I think the most surprising is the traversal between sky, to the land of Hyrule and even to the underground is seamless with no loading screens between. You can dive from the sky islands straight into a chasm leading to the underground without any issues. Its pretty impressive and it shows how much polish and thought the developers put into the game. They've redone the music and sound system, providing a better experience and adding awesome musical scores that really add to the experience. Overall, this is game of the the year material. I highly recommend everyone pick this up and play.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom

author: JokerPilot
quote: As a fan of Hyrule warriors, I was excited for another chapter in the blossoming series and when I learned it was taking place 100 years prior to botw, I was beyond excited! While the game may have it's moments dipping down in fps(I'm looking at you Urbosa's special) it doesn't detract from the fun. The dips that happen are very few and last only mere seconds that it's very easy to ignore, especially when you're busy trying to finish your tasks before the time limit expires. The story is really good and the voice acting is absolutely amazing. It made the journey around Hyrule memorable. Truthfully I think i prefered the bosses in AoC over Botw. I hope everyone will give this a chance so they too can experience the journey.

author: JokerPilot
quote:
The only reason this game is even getting this type of score is because the music is really good.

PROS:
- Good visuals
- Great music
- Good base for an actual good game

CONS
- An over complicated ring battle system that makes it annoying to do battles at all.
- Battles don't give any XP, making them basically useless to do at all!
- The only original designs is Olivia and Olly
- Partners are only temporary and not really part of the adventure
- They still are leaning on that sticker star system, though not as heavily, items are temporary
- The constant paper gimmicks thrown in your face is getting tiresome
- The bosses literally are office supplies, who even approved this idea at all???
- There is no RPG system, no partners that stay with you, they lost a lot of their originality.
- NPCs lost a lot of their originality - Botw and Mario Odyssey have original characters, why can't Paper Mario???

Overall - A waste of money, only buy this game if its on sale for cheap or watch a youtuber gameplay it. Its not worth it. The writing is ok, but there is only so much paper gimmick jokes you can take. It makes me sad cause Mario RPG, Paper Mario 64, and The Thousand Year Door, had beautiful amazing original characters, great story, beautiful worlds that didn't focus on the Paper gimmick, a great soundtrack, meaningful battles that made the player feel stronger as you progressed since there is XP(and you had to manage your HP, FP, and Badge Points as you leveled up), Badges that gave you ways to customize that experience and great partners that shared the story/adventure with you. These are things which I feel is completely lost in the newer series. I urge others to play Mario RPG, Paper Mario 64 and The Thousand Year Door over this game because you'll get a better more fulfilling adventure then you would here.
